name: mcap
desc: Serialization-agnostic container file format for pub/sub messages
why: Robotics log container format with a neat self-describing design, but it is a file format more than a door into something alive.

brief.what_it_is: MCAP (pronounced "em-cap") is an open source container file format and logging library for multimodal, timestamped log data. It stores multiple channels of pre-serialized messages in one file, and the README says it is commonly used in robotics. Input is messages from pub/sub or sensor streams in any binary encoding; output is a single MCAP file that can be read back with the language libraries or the mcap CLI, which can inspect, merge, and split files.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches MCAP as a way to record and replay pub/sub and multimodal sensor logs regardless of serialization format, and says it is designed for robotics and pub/sub use. The GitHub README describes it as a logging library and file format that works under various workloads, resource constraints, and durability requirements.
brief.how_it_works: Files are row-oriented and append-only, which the homepage says minimizes disk I/O and reduces corruption risk on unclean shutdowns. Message schemas are stored alongside the data so files stay readable as code changes. Optional features include an index for fast seeking, chunk-based compression with LZ4 or Zstandard, and CRC checksums, which the homepage says can be configured per application. The format is specified at mcap.dev/spec and has a Kaitai Struct definition in the repo.

commands_seen.context: Install command given in the GitHub README for the MCAP CLI, used to inspect, merge, and split MCAP files.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install mcap, the README points to the GitHub releases page (github.com/foxglove/mcap/releases?q=cli) for downloading the CLI directly. Libraries are installed through each language's package manager: pip package mcap for Python, npm @mcap/core for TypeScript, crates.io mcap for Rust, Conan mcap for C++, and Go and Swift via releases. The CLI guide at mcap.dev/guides/cli covers installation and usage, but I did not fetch it. No hardware, accounts, or first-run configuration were mentioned.
brief.standout: The file is self-describing: schemas live inside the file, so it stays readable without the original code, and the serialization is left to the user. The homepage also says MCAP is the default log format in ROS 2, which is a notable adoption claim for a file format.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage and README are current in tone and link to a maintained-looking docs set, and the homepage says it is used in production. I did not see a last release date or last commit date in the pages I fetched, so I cannot confirm activity. The project is a Foxglove project.
brief.caveats: This is a file format and libraries, not a service or app, so there is little to try interactively beyond the CLI. The README's CLI section is brief and I did not check the CLI guide for supported platforms. The homepage's 'Trusted by leading robotics teams' section lists logos only in text form, so company claims are unverified. Licensed MIT per the README.
